# GAPS — symfony-demo audit

**GENERATED by `tools/audit/rank.php`. Do not edit.**
Evidence is under `docs/audit/data/` and `docs/audit/probes/`; the severity,
depth and ownership calls are in `docs/audit/findings.tsv`. `rank.php --check`
regenerates this file and fails on any difference, so nothing here is a claim
without a file behind it.

## Severity classes

| class | meaning |
|---|---|
| S0 | **silent wrong answer** — compiles, links, runs, answers differently than php. Ranked above everything because it poisons every other measurement: a green build is actively misleading. |
| S1 | runtime hard failure — crash, uncaught throw, or a `return 0` link-stub that explodes later |
| S2 | compile or link hard failure, or a compiler crash |
| S3 | static finding with no observed runtime effect |
| S4 | advisory / analyzer residue |

**22 findings**: 1 S0, 1 S1, 10 S2, 8 S3, 2 S4.

Capability probes: 9 COMPILE, 1 CRASH, 9 DIFF, 7 PASS (`docs/audit/data/capability.tsv`).

one that was never written. Each carries the probe that now gates it —
the promotion rule from `README.md` moves a probe into `tests/aot/cases/`
in the same commit that closes its gap.

|---|---|---|---|

| `ffi-alias-capture-nul` | `bare-alias-capture` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_str_capture_family.php` | strcmp/strncmp/strcasecmp/strncasecmp compared NUL-terminated, so strcmp("a\0b","a\0c") answered 0 — now length-aware, unsigned, with PHP's prefix rule |
| `empty-array-byref-elem-repr` | `element-repr` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_callback_byref_capture.php` | an erased local passed to a by-ref callee that appends a foreign kind stayed vec[unknown] — collectByRefWidenArgs skipped UNKNOWN, deferring to an INTRA-procedural scan that cannot see the callee's store |
| `erased-byref-closure-capture` | `element-repr` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_array_recursion.php` | the widen scan walked CALL args only, so a `use (&$erased)` capture was an invisible by-ref writer; it now walks Closure_ captures too, and an append whose provenance is not visible at the site (a closure own param, supplied by the invoker) widens an erased element rather than being given the benefit of the doubt |
| `preg-named-groups` | `regex-surface` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_preg_named_groups.php` | no named group ever reached $matches in preg_match or preg_match_all — PCRE2's name table was never read; pcre2_pattern_info is now bound and the name is interleaved ahead of its number, as php does |
| `preg-offset-capture-pair` | `regex-surface` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_preg_named_groups.php` | preg_match ignored $flags entirely; PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE and PREG_UNMATCHED_AS_NULL now behave (preg_match_all already handled OFFSET_CAPTURE — the original finding conflated the two functions) |
| `union-nullable-loses-class` | `type-lowering` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_union_nullable_class.php` | lowerTypeHint sent every hint containing `|` to a cell, so the union spelling of a nullable (`S|null`, identical to `?S` in php) lost its class — the static type became bare `object` and every dispatch keyed on it misfired. Not prelude-specific: prelude/reflection.php just happens to spell all four optional returns that way |
| `shutdown-order-and-args` | `lifecycle` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_destruct_and_shutdown.php` | the queue ran only from an atexit hook, so it fired AFTER main returned and after every trailing release had run its destructors; and register_shutdown_function dropped its ...$args, so a callback parameter read an unbound slot |
| `iterator-double-foreach-sigbus` | `iteration` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_iterator_protocol.php` | MISNAMED, and the name cost the time: the two foreach loops were always correct and match the interpreter byte for byte. Splitting the probe into one statement per file put the SIGBUS on iterator_to_array, which routed every non-array argument into a \Generator-typed funnel — so an IteratorAggregate was read as a generator frame, its refcount taken for the state word and its class DESCRIPTOR pointer loaded from slot 0 and called, jumping into a read-only data page. The title was inherited from a memory note about a different crash and never bisected; the recorded evidence was rc>128 with an empty stdout, which says nothing about WHERE, because the harness block-buffers to a file and a fatal signal discards the buffer |
| `traversable-implicit-base` | `iteration` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_iterator_protocol.php` | found by the same probe's last line: `$bag instanceof Traversable` was false for a class implementing IteratorAggregate. classIsA matches a target against a class's OWN interface list and then walks parents, but Iterator and IteratorAggregate are built-ins absent from the class table, so the walk never reached their implicit base. php forbids implementing Traversable directly, so those two are the whole membership rule — modelled the way Stringable already was |
| `include-returns-null` | `include-semantics` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_include_returns_value/main.php` | the parser consumed the path operand and returned Expr::null, so `$x = require 'config.php'` was always null. Whole-program AOT already compiles the target's declarations in and already runs its top-level statements inline, so the LOAD was genuinely redundant — the VALUE was not. Each non-entry file's top-level `return` now stores into a per-file global instead of being dropped, and require/include resolves a path to that slot through a strcmp chain over the closed file set, comparing REALPATHs so the several spellings a program reaches one file by all match. No execution-order change: this is the eager model, chosen over lazy per-file units precisely because it does not move when any vendor file's top-level code runs |
| `func-args-absent` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_func_args.php` | the finding said absent; measuring said worse. func_num_args() was CONSTANT-FOLDED to the declared parameter count, so a three-optional function answered 3 for every call including the zero-argument one, and func_get_arg($i) with a non-literal index (the idiomatic loop) fell through to an undefined symbol. The count now rides a demand-gated side channel: the call site pushes what the SOURCE wrote before defaultFillArgs pads it, and the callee takes it in its first statement. Not a hidden parameter — the closure struct is fixed-arity and an indirect call could not carry one. Arguments written past the declared list ride a companion slot, which is what SymfonyStyle::comment() needs when it declares one parameter and reads func_get_arg(1) |
| `sapi-fns-absent` | `sapi-layer` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_sapi_fn_presence.php` | closed by the main merge (prelude sapi.php + session.php + ob.php) plus putenv and php_sapi_name here — header/header_remove/headers_sent/headers_list/http_response_code/setcookie/setrawcookie, the session_* family, the ob_* family and the error-handler family all exist and were re-verified by CALLING them, not by asking after them. Only php WARNINGS differ (headers already sent), which is the north-star no-warnings divergence and not a gap in this surface |
| `function-exists-prelude-gated` | `error-handling` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_sapi_fn_presence.php` | function_exists('<literal>') answered FALSE for 23 names that plainly work — the whole header/session/ob/error-handler surface. functionIsKnown consulted what the prelude HAD declared, but the prelude is demand-gated on a mention that looks like use, and a name appearing only inside function_exists deliberately does not create demand: the predicate was measuring its own gate rather than the language. It now also consults what the prelude WOULD declare, a hardcoded set that calibrate.sh derives from prelude/*.php and fails on drift. Safe in the direction that matters — a program that goes on to CALL the name makes a real mention, which injects the file |
| `putenv-absent` | `sapi-layer` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_putenv.php` | putenv now a codegen builtin over libc setenv/unsetenv. No shadow table, and that is why it round-trips: getenv reads the real environ and $_SERVER/$_ENV are built from it, so one store is visible to all three. setenv/unsetenv rather than C putenv, which takes ownership of a buffer this compiler will free. The name must be copied into its own NUL-terminated buffer — splitting in place by writing over the = is what C does and is UB here, because the argument is usually a string LITERAL, so LLVM kept the original bytes and setenv got NAME=value as the name, which is EINVAL: putenv answered false and set nothing |
| `array-walk-recursive-callback` | `element-repr` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_array_recursion.php` | array_walk_recursive handed its callback values that read back as raw bits — a witness of erased-byref-closure-capture, closed with it; array_push into an erased local was the same bug and is closed too |
| `parser-xor-operator` | `parser-gaps` | `tests/aot/cases/word_operators.php` | closed on main by cf74105 (`and`/`or`/`xor`), not by this branch — re-verified byte-exact after the merge |
| `parser-reserved-enum-case` | `parser-gaps` | `tests/aot/cases/reserved_member_names.php` | a reserved word may name a class constant or an enum case in php; the lexer emits Keyword and the parser demanded Identifier. expectMemberName() accepts both, and only in member position — `class array` stays a syntax error |
| `parser-high-byte-identifier` | `parser-gaps` | `tests/aot/cases/high_byte_identifier.php` | two halves: isIdentStart admitted ASCII only (php grammar is [a-zA-Z_\x80-\xff]), and once parsed the raw bytes reached the LLVM symbol — mangle/sanitizeSym now hex-escape any byte >= 0x80 |
| `parser-const-gaps` | `parser-gaps` | `tests/aot/cases/reserved_member_names.php` | same root as parser-reserved-enum-case — the const-name positions demanded Identifier where php allows a reserved word |

## By owning epic

The ladder tier is the implementation order: a tier's dependency closure
lies entirely in lower tiers, so a gap first seen at tier N blocks tiers
N..8 and nothing below.

### `error-handling` — 3 finding(s), first bites at T0

- **S0** `function-exists-dynamic-arg` — function_exists($var) with a NON-literal argument folds to false for EVERY function, builtins included: a loop over a list of names reports strlen, count and floor all missing. Documented in LowerExprs as a conservative fold, but conservative is the wrong word for an answer that is simply wrong — and it is not theoretical, it is what made this audit's own SAPI presence probe report trigger_error and ob_start missing and nearly bought a second false finding. The function set is CLOSED at compile time, so the fix is the shape emitDynFnCall and the include resolver already use: a name table plus a runtime scan
- **S3** `diagnostic-format-vs-php` — difftest flags error_handler_basic and trigger_deprecation_shape, and both are pure diagnostic FORMAT: php CLI emits every notice TWICE (once prefixed `PHP Notice:  `, once `Notice: `) and names the file by ABSOLUTE path, while manticore emits once with the path as written. The suite passes because its expected files encode our shape; only raw php parity sees it. Pre-existing, and adjacent to the no-warnings-throw-exceptions north star rather than a bug under it
- **S3** `function-exists-lies` — NEARLY CLOSED: was 44 of 53 common functions answering false; now 5. Fixed by teaching functionIsKnown the codegen builtins, the rest of the emitBuiltin dispatch and the compiler rewrites. The 5 left are DEMAND-GATED prelude names (error_reporting, register_shutdown_function, set_error_handler, ob_start, ob_get_clean) that the program only MENTIONS inside function_exists without calling — the prelude is then never injected.
